p0.zh: 积极外部因素和公共物品介绍

p2.original: The Benefits of Voyager I Endure

p3.original: The rapid growth of technology has increased our ability to access and process data, to navigate through a busy city, and to communicate with friends on the other side of the globe. The research and development efforts of citizens, scientists, firms, universities, and governments have truly revolutionized the modern economy. To get a sense of how far we have come in a short period of time, let’s compare one of humankind’s greatest achievements to the smartphone.
p3.zh: 技术的迅速发展提高了我们获取和处理数据,在繁忙的城市航行,以及同地球另一边的朋友进行交流的能力。公民,科学家,企业,大学,政府的研发努力,真正实现了现代经济的革命性. 让我们将人类最伟大的成就之一与智能手机相比较。

p4.original: In 1977 the United States launched Voyager I, a spacecraft originally intended to reach Jupiter and Saturn, to send back photographs and other cosmic measurements. Voyager I, however, kept going, and going—past Jupiter and Saturn—right out of our solar system. At the time of its launch, Voyager had some of the most sophisticated computing processing power NASA could engineer (8,000 instructions per second), but today, we Earthlings use handheld devices that can process 14 billion instructions per second.
p4.zh: 1977年,美国发射了Voyager I号,该航天器原本打算飞到木星和土星,以送回照片和其他宇宙测量. 然而,Voyager I继续前进,然后继续前进——过去木星和土星——离开我们的太阳系。 在发射时,Voyager拥有一些NASA可以制造的最先进的计算处理能力(每秒8,000个指令),但今天,我们地球人使用手持设备,每秒可以处理140亿个指令.

p5.original: Still, the technology of today is a spillover product of the incredible feats NASA accomplished over forty years ago. NASA research, for instance, is responsible for the kidney dialysis and mammogram machines that we use today. Research in new technologies not only produces private benefits to the investing firm, or in this case to NASA, but it also creates benefits for the broader society. In this way, new knowledge often becomes what economists refer to as a public good. This leads us to the topic of this chapter—technology, positive externalities, public goods, and the role of government in encouraging innovation and the social benefits that it provides.
p5.zh: 然而,今天的技术是美国航天局40年前完成的令人难以置信的功绩的外溢产物。 例如,NASA的研究负责我们今天使用的肾透析和乳房X线照相机。新技术的研究不仅为投资公司带来私人利益,或在此情况下为美国航天局带来利益,而且还为更广泛的社会带来利益. 这样,新知识往往成为经济学家所称的公益物. 这使我们想到本章的主题——技术、积极的外在因素、公益物以及政府在鼓励创新和提供社会效益方面的作用。

p6.original: Introduction to Positive Externalities and Public Goods
p6.zh: 积极外部因素和公共物品介绍

p7.original: In this chapter, you will learn about:

p8.original: Why the Private Sector Underinvests in Technologies
p8.zh: 为什么私营部门在技术方面的投资不足

p11.original: As economist Mariana Mazzucato explores in her well-known work The Entrepreneurial State, what makes a smartphone smart? What allows its apps to help you navigate new towns while getting updates about your home, all while your hands are on the steering wheel and your children are in the back seat watching their shows? For starters, the internet, cell tower networks, GPS, and voice activation. Each of these, and many other technologies we rely on, were developed with intensive government support. For example, GPS, which enables many cell phone functions beyond the frequently used mapping and ride-sharing applications, was developed by the U.S. Department of Defense over several generations of satellite tracking and complex computer algorithm development. The U.S. government still provides GPS for many of the world’s users.
p11.zh: 正如经济学家Mariana Mazzucato在她著名的作品《创业国家》中探索的那样, 智能手机的智能化是什么?是什么让你的应用在获得关于你家的最新消息的同时 帮助你驾驭新城镇? 当你手放在方向盘上,孩子坐在后座上看他们的节目时? 首先,互联网,手机塔网络,GPS,和语音激活。 这些技术以及我们所依赖的许多其他技术都是在政府的大力支持下开发的。 例如,GPS使得许多手机功能超越了常用的映射和骑行共享应用,是美国开发的.国防部历经数代卫星跟踪和复杂的计算机算法开发.美国政府仍然为世界上许多用户提供GPS.

p12.original: We do not often think of the government when we consider our leading products and entrepreneurs. We think of Apple, Google, Lyft, Tesla, Fitbit, and so on—creative innovators who built on the tools provided by these government efforts, using them in transformative ways. We may not think of the estimated $19 billion per year that the U.S. spends to maintain the GPS system, but we would certainly think of it if it suddenly went away. (Beyond the impact on our daily lives, economists estimate U.S. businesses alone would lose about $1 billion per day without GPS.)
p12.zh: 当我们考虑我们的主要产品和企业家时,我们并不经常想到政府。 我们想到苹果、谷歌、莱夫特、特斯拉、菲特比特等创新者, 我们可能不会想到美国每年花费大约190亿美元来维持GPS系统,但是如果它突然消失,我们当然会想到这一点.(除了对我们日常生活的影响之外,经济学家估计,没有全球定位系统,光是美国的企业每天就损失约10亿美元。)

p13.original: Mazzucato is one of several prominent economists advocating for an embrace of continued government-sponsored innovations in order to build economic prosperity, reduce inequality, and manage ongoing challenges such as drought, coastal changes, and extreme weather. She argues that competitive, private sector markets are often resistant to the risks involved with large-scale innovation, because failed experiments and lack of uptake lead to massive corporate and personal losses. Governments can take on riskier research and development projects. Because government spending is fueled by taxpayers, and all innovation leads to some level of employment change, these proposals are certainly complex and challenging to implement.
p13.zh: Mazzucato是几位知名经济学家之一, 主张接受政府持续赞助的创新, 以建立经济繁荣、减少不平等、管理干旱、沿海变化、极端气候等持续挑战。 她争辩说,竞争性的私营部门市场往往抵制大规模创新的风险,因为失败的实验和缺乏吸收会导致企业和个人的巨大损失。 政府可以承担更危险的研究和发展项目。 由于政府支出由纳税人推动,而且所有创新都会导致一定程度的就业变化,这些建议无疑是复杂和难以执行的。

p14.original: This chapter deals with some of these issues: Will private companies be willing to invest in new technology? In what ways does new technology have positive externalities? What motivates inventors? What role should government play in encouraging research and technology? Are there certain types of goods that markets fail to provide efficiently, and that only government can produce? What happens when consumption or production of a product creates positive externalities? Why is it unsurprising when we overuse a common resource, like marine fisheries?
p14.zh: 本章讨论其中一些问题:私营公司是否愿意投资于新技术?新技术以什么方式具有积极的外部性? 什么激励发明者?政府在鼓励研究和技术方面应发挥什么作用?是否有市场不能有效提供的某些种类的商品,只有政府才能生产? 当一种产品的消费或生产产生积极的外部效应时会发生什么情况? 当我们过度使用共同资源,如海洋渔业时,为什么并不奇怪?

p16.original: Market competition can provide an incentive for discovering new technology because a firm can earn higher profits by finding a way to produce products more cheaply or to create products with characteristics consumers want. As Gregory Lee, CEO of Samsung said, “Relentless pursuit of new innovation is the key principle of our business and enables consumers to discover a world of possibilities with technology.” An innovative firm knows that it will usually have a temporary edge over its competitors and thus an ability to earn above-normal profits before competitors can catch up.
p16.zh: 市场竞争可以为发现新技术提供一种激励,因为公司可以通过找到一种方法,以更廉价的方式生产产品或创造消费者想要的具有特点的产品,从而获得更高的利润。 正如三星总裁Gregory Lee所说 , “ 毫不松懈地追求新的创新是我们企业的关键原则,并且使消费者能够发现一个有技术的可能性的世界。 ”创新企业知道,它通常会拥有一个超越竞争对手的临时优势,因此在竞争对手能够赶超之前能够赚取高于正常的利润。

p17.original: In certain cases, however, competition can discourage new technology, especially when other firms can quickly copy a new idea. Consider a pharmaceutical firm deciding to develop a new drug. On average, it can cost $800 million and take more than a decade to discover a new drug, perform the necessary safety tests, and bring the drug to market. If the research and development (R&D) effort fails—and every R&D project has some chance of failure—then the firm will suffer losses and could even be driven out of business. If the project succeeds, then the firm’s competitors may figure out ways of adapting and copying the underlying idea, but without having to pay the costs themselves. As a result, the innovative company will bear the much higher costs of the R&D and will enjoy at best only a small, temporary advantage over the competition.
p17.zh: 然而,在某些情况下,竞争会阻碍新技术,特别是当其他公司能够迅速复制新想法时。考虑一个制药公司 决定开发一种新药物。平均来说,可以花费8亿美元,需要十多年的时间才能发现一种新药物,进行必要的安全检测,并将该药物带入市场. 如果研发工作失败——每个研发项目都有失败的可能——那么公司将遭受损失,甚至可能被赶出企业。 如果项目成功,那么公司的竞争者可能想出一些方法来修改和复制基本的想法,但不必自己支付费用。 因此,创新型公司将承担研发成本高得多的费用,最多只能享有比竞争小的暂时优势.

p18.original: Many inventors over the years have discovered that their inventions brought them less profit than they might have reasonably expected.
p18.zh: 多年来许多发明家发现他们的发明给他们带来的利润比他们合理的预期要少.

p19.original: Eli Whitney (1765–1825) invented the cotton gin, but then southern cotton planters built their own seed-separating devices with a few minor changes in Whitney’s design. When Whitney sued, he found that the courts in southern states would not uphold his patent rights.
p19.zh: Eli Whitney(1765–1825)发明了棉花杜松子酒,但后来南方棉厂商自己制造了种子分离装置,对Whitney的设计略作改动. 在惠特尼起诉时,他发现南方各州的法院不会维护他的专利权.

p20.original: Thomas Edison (1847–1931) still holds the record for most patents granted to an individual. His first invention was an automatic vote counter, and despite the social benefits, he could not find a government that wanted to buy it.
p20.zh: 托马斯·爱迪生(1847–1931)仍然保持着授予个人的大多数专利的记录. 他的第一个发明是自动投票计数器,尽管有社会福利,他还是找不到一个想要购买它的政府.

p21.original: Gordon Gould came up with the idea behind the laser in 1957. He put off applying for a patent and, by the time he did apply, other scientists had laser inventions of their own. A lengthy legal battle resulted, in which Gould spent $100,000 on lawyers, before he eventually received a patent for the laser in 1977. Compared to the enormous social benefits of the laser, Gould received relatively little financial reward.
p21.zh: 1957年戈登·古尔德提出了激光背后的想法. 他推迟申请专利,到他申请时,其他科学家也拥有自己的激光发明.一场漫长的法律战由此而来,古尔德在律师身上花费了10万美元,直到他最终在1977年获得了激光专利.与激光的巨大社会效益相比,古尔德获得的财政奖励相对较少.

p22.original: In 1936, Alan Turing delivered a paper titled, "On Computable Numbers, with an Application to the Entscheidungsproblem," in which he presented the notion of a universal machine (later called the “Universal Turing Machine," and then the "Turing machine") capable of computing anything that is computable. The central concept of the modern computer was based on Turing’s paper. Today scholars widely consider Turing as the father of theoretical computer science and artificial intelligence; however, the UK government prosecuted Turing in 1952 for engaging in same-sex sexual acts and gave him the choice of chemical castration or prison. Turing chose castration and died in 1954 from cyanide poisoning.
p22.zh: 1936年,艾伦·图灵递交了一篇题为“关于可计算数字, 并带有适用于Entscheidungs problem的应用程序”的论文, 其中他提出了一种通用机器(后来称为“通用图灵机器”,然后称为“图灵机器”)的概念,能够计算任何可计算的东西。现代计算机的中心概念是基于图灵的论文. 今天学者普遍认为图灵是理论计算机科学和人工智能的父辈;然而,英国政府于1952年起诉图灵从事同性性行为,并让他选择化学阉割或监禁. 图灵选择阉割,1954年死于氰化物中毒.

p23.original: A variety of studies by economists have found that the original inventor receives one-third to one-half of the total economic benefits from innovations, while other businesses and new product users receive the rest.
p23.zh: 经济学家的各种研究发现,原发明人从创新中获得的经济利益占总经济利益的三分之一至一半,而其他企业和新产品使用者则获得其余的.

p24.original: The Positive Externalities of New Technology

p25.original: Will private firms in a market economy underinvest in research and technology? If a firm builds a factory or buys a piece of equipment, the firm receives all the economic benefits that result from the investments. However, when a firm invests in new technology, the private benefits, or profits, that the firm receives are only a portion of the overall social benefits. The social benefits of an innovation account for the value of all the positive externalities of the new idea or product, whether enjoyed by other companies or society as a whole, as well as the private benefits the firm that developed the new technology receives. As you learned in Environmental Protection and Negative Externalities, positive externalities are beneficial spillovers to a third party, or parties.
p25.zh: 市场经济中的私营公司是否会对研究和技术投资不足? 如果一家公司建造工厂或购买设备,则该公司从投资中获得所有经济利益。 然而,当一家公司对新技术进行投资时,公司获得的私人利益或利润只是整体社会福利的一部分。创新的社会效益反映了新思想或产品的所有积极外部效应的价值,无论是其他公司还是整个社会所享受的,以及开发新技术的公司所获得的私人利益。 正如你从环境保护和负面外部学到的,积极的外部效应对第三方或各方都是有利的外溢。

p26.original: Consider the example of the Big Drug Company, which is planning its R&D budget for the next year. Economists and scientists working for Big Drug have compiled a list of potential research and development projects and estimated rates of return. (The rate of return is the estimated payoff from the project.)  shows how the calculations work. The downward-sloping DPrivate curve represents the firm’s demand for financial capital and reflects the company’s willingness to borrow to finance research and development projects at various interest rates. Suppose that this firm’s investment in research and development creates a spillover benefit to other firms and households. After all, new innovations often spark other creative endeavors that society also values. If we add the spillover benefits society enjoys to the firm’s private demand for financial capital, we can draw DSocial that lies above DPrivate.
p26.zh: 以大药公司为例,该公司正在规划下一年的研发预算。 为大药店工作的经济学家和科学家汇编了一份潜在研发项目清单和估计收益率。(收益率是项目的估计收益。 )显示计算如何进行。向下倾斜的私人曲线代表了公司对金融资本的需求,并反映了公司愿意以各种利率借款资助研发项目。假设该公司对研发的投资会给其他公司和家庭带来溢出利益。毕竟,新的创新往往激发社会也珍视的其他创造性努力。 如果我们把溢出效应的好处加到公司私人对金融资本的需求上,我们就可以吸引超越私人的DSocial。

p27.original: If there were a way for the firm to fully monopolize those social benefits by somehow making them unavailable to the rest of us, the firm’s private demand curve would be the same as society’s demand curve. According to  and , if the going rate of interest on borrowing is 8%, and the company can receive the private benefits of innovation only, then the company would finance $30 million. Society, at the same rate of 8%, would find it optimal to have $52 million of borrowing. Unless there is a way for the company to fully enjoy the total benefits, then it will borrow less than the socially optimal level of $52 million.
p27.zh: 如果公司有办法通过某种方式使我们其他人得不到这些社会福利来完全垄断这些社会福利,那么公司的私人需求曲线将与社会的需求曲线相同。并且,如果借款的利率为8%,而公司只能获得创新的私人利益,那么公司将出资3000万美元.以8%的同样利率,社会认为拥有5 200万美元的借款是最佳的。 除非公司有办法充分享受全部利益,否则,公司借款将低于社会最佳水平的5200万美元。

p28.zh: B. 积极外部因素和技术

p48.original: Big Drug’s original demand for financial capital (DPrivate) is based on the profits the firm receives. However, other pharmaceutical firms and health care companies may learn new lessons about how to treat certain medical conditions and are then able to create their own competing products. The social benefit of the drug takes into account the value of all the drug's positive externalities. If Big Drug were able to gain this social return instead of other companies, its demand for financial capital would shift to the demand curve DSocial, and it would be willing to borrow and invest $52 million. However, if Big Drug is receiving only 50 cents of each dollar of social benefits, the firm will not spend as much on creating new products. The amount it would be willing to spend would fall somewhere in between DPrivate and DSocial.
p48.zh: 大药店最初对金融资本(Dprivate)的需求是基于该公司获得的利润。 然而,其他制药公司和保健公司可能从如何治疗某些医疗条件方面吸取新的教训,然后能够创造自己的竞争产品。药物的社会效益考虑到药物所有正外观的价值. 如果大毒品公司能够而不是其他公司获得这种社会回报,那么其对金融资本的需求将转移到需求曲线DSocial,它愿意借款和投资5200万美元. 然而,如果大药店只得到每美元50美分的社会福利,那么公司不会花那么多钱来创造新产品. 它愿意花的金额会在私人和社会之间。

p50.original: The investment in anything, whether it is the construction of a new power plant or research in a new cancer treatment, usually requires a certain upfront cost with an uncertain future benefit. The investment in education, or human capital, is no different. Over the span of many years, a student and her family invest significant amounts of time and money into that student’s education. The idea is that higher levels of educational attainment will eventually serve to increase the student’s future productivity and subsequent ability to earn. Once the student crunches the numbers, does this investment pay off for her?
p50.zh: 投资任何东西,无论是建造新电厂,还是研究新癌症治疗,通常都需要一定的预付成本,未来收益不确定.教育投资,或人力资本投资,并无不同。多年来,一名学生及其家人为学生的教育投入了大量的时间和资金。其理念是,提高教育水平最终将有助于提高学生未来的生产力和随后的挣钱能力。 一旦学生压缩数字,这种投资是否为她带来回报?

p51.original: Almost universally, economists have found that the answer to this question is a clear “Yes.” For example, several studies of the return to education in the United States estimate that the rate of return to a college education is approximately 10-15%. Data in , from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics’ Usual Weekly Earnings of Wage and Salary Workers, Fourth Quarter 2021, demonstrate that median weekly earnings are higher for workers who have completed more education. While these rates of return will beat equivalent investments in Treasury bonds or savings accounts, the estimated returns to education go primarily to the individual worker, so these returns are private rates of return to education.
p51.zh: 经济学家们几乎都认为这一问题的答案是明确的“是 ” 。 例如,美国一些关于恢复教育的研究估计,恢复大学教育的比率约为10-15%。数据来自美国劳工统计局的《工资和薪金工人的每周收入》,第4季度,2021年,显示完成更多教育的工人的每周收入中位数较高。 虽然这些收益率将比国库债券或储蓄账户的同等投资高,但估计的教育收益主要归于工人个人,因此这些收益是私人的教育收益率。

p52.original: Usual Weekly Earnings of Wage and Salary Workers, Fourth Quarter 2021
p52.zh: 2021年第四季度工资和薪金工人的每周收入

p57.original: Median Weekly Earnings (full-time workers over the age of 25)
p57.zh: 中等周收入(25岁以上的全职工人)

p61.original: What does society gain from investing in the education of another student? After all, if the government is spending taxpayer dollars to subsidize public education, society should expect some kind of return on that spending. Economists like George Psacharopoulos have found that, across a variety of nations, the social rate of return on schooling is also positive. After all, positive externalities exist from investment in education. While not always easy to measure, according to Walter McMahon, the positive externalities to education typically include better health outcomes for the population, lower levels of crime, a cleaner environment and a more stable, democratic government. For these reasons, many nations have chosen to use taxpayer dollars to subsidize primary, secondary, and higher education. Education clearly benefits the person who receives it, but a society where most people have a good level of education provides positive externalities for all.
p61.zh: 社会从对另一个学生的教育投资中得到了什么好处?毕竟,如果政府用纳税人的美元来补贴公共教育,社会应该期望这种开支得到某种回报.乔治·普萨罗普洛斯(George Psacharopoulos)等经济学家发现,在不同国家,学校教育的社会回报率也是积极的.归根结底,教育投资是积极的外在因素。瓦尔特·麦克马洪认为,教育的积极外在因素虽然并不总是容易衡量,但通常包括人民健康效果更好、犯罪率较低、环境更清洁以及政府更稳定、更民主。 由于这些原因,许多国家选择使用纳税人美元补贴初等、中等和高等教育。教育显然使接受教育的人受益,但大多数人受教育程度良好的社会为所有人提供了积极的外部条件。

p62.zh: 积极外部因素的其他例子

p63.original: Although technology may be the most prominent example of a positive externality, it is not the only one. For example, vaccinations against disease are not only a protection for the individual, but they have the positive spillover of protecting others who may become infected.  When a number of homes in a neighborhood are modernized, updated, and restored, not only does it increase the homes' value, but other property values in the neighborhood may increase as well.
p63.zh: 虽然技术可能是积极外部性最突出的例子,但它并非是唯一的例子。 例如,预防疾病的接种不仅对个人是一种保护,而且具有保护可能感染的其他人的积极外溢作用。 当一个街区的一些住宅实现现代化,更新,并恢复时,不仅会增加住宅的价值,而且该街区的其他财产价值也会增加.

p64.original: The appropriate public policy response to a positive externality, like a new technology, is to help the party creating the positive externality receive a greater share of the social benefits. In the case of vaccines, like flu shots, an effective policy might be to provide a subsidy to those who choose to get vaccinated.
p64.zh: 对积极的外部性,像新技术一样,适当的公共政策对策是帮助创造积极的外部性一方获得更大的社会收益份额。 就疫苗而言,如流感疫苗,有效的政策可能是向那些选择接种疫苗的人提供补贴。

p65.original: shows the market for flu shots. The market demand curve DMarket for flu shots reflects only the marginal private benefits (MPB) that the vaccinated individuals receive from the shots. Assuming that there are no spillover costs in the production of flu shots, the market supply curve is given by the marginal private cost (MPC) of producing the vaccinations.
p65.zh: 显示流感的市场。市场需求曲线DMarket的流感疫苗只反映了接种疫苗者从疫苗中获得的边际私人利益(MPB)。假设在生产流感疫苗时没有外溢成本,那么市场供应曲线是由生产疫苗的边际私人成本(MPC)给出的.

p66.original: The equilibrium quantity of flu shots produced in the market, where MPB is equal to MPC, is QMarket and the price of flu shots is PMarket. However, spillover benefits exist in this market because others, those who chose not to purchase a flu shot, receive a positive externality in the form of a reduced chance of contracting the flu. When we add the spillover benefits to the marginal private benefit of flu shots, the marginal social benefit (MSB) of flu shots is given by DSocial. Because the MSB is greater than MPB, we see that the socially optimal level of flu shots is greater than the market quantity (QSocial exceeds QMarket) and the corresponding price of flu shots, if the market were to produce QSocial, would be at PSocial. Unfortunately, the marketplace does not recognize the positive externality and flu shots will go under-produced and under-consumed.
p66.zh: 市场上生产的流感镜头的平衡数量,其中MPB等于MPC,是QMarket,流感镜头的价格是PMarket. 然而,在这个市场中存在溢出效应,因为其他人,那些选择不购买流感疫苗的人,以降低感染流感的机会的形式获得积极的外部作用. 当我们将溢出利益加到流感的边缘私人利益上时,流感的边缘社会利益(MSB)由DSocial给予. 由于MSB比MPB大,我们看到社会上最佳水平的流感镜头比市场数量大(QSocial 超过QMarket),如果市场要生产QSocial的话,相应的流感镜头价格将会在PSocial. 不幸的是,市场没有认识到积极的外部性,流感的发病量将不足和消费不足。

p67.original: How can government try to move the market level of output closer to the socially desirable level of output? One policy would be to provide a subsidy, like a voucher, to any citizen who wishes to get vaccinated. This voucher would act as “income” that one could use to purchase only a flu shot and, if the voucher were exactly equal to the per-unit spillover benefits, would increase market equilibrium to a quantity of QSocial and a price of PSocial where MSB equals MSC (which equals MPC given the assumption that there are no spillover costs in producing the vaccine). Suppliers of the flu shots would receive payment of PSocial per vaccination, while consumers of flu shots would redeem the voucher and only pay a price of PSubsidy. When the government uses a subsidy in this way, it produces the socially optimal quantity of vaccinations.
p67.zh: 政府如何设法使产出的市场水平更接近社会所期望的产出水平?一项政策是,向任何希望接种疫苗的公民提供补贴,就像一种优惠券。 这种凭证将是一种“收入”,人们只能用来购买流感疫苗,如果凭证与单位外溢效益完全相同,就会将市场平衡提高到一定数量的QSocial和PSocial的价格,其中MSC等于MSC(由于假设疫苗生产没有外溢成本).流感疫苗的供应商每次接种疫苗都会收到PSocial的付款,而流感疫苗的消费者则会赎回券,只支付PSubsidy的价格. 当政府以这种方式使用补贴时,它会产生社会上最优的疫苗接种量.

p68.original: The Market for Flu Shots with Spillover Benefits (A Positive Externality)
p68.zh: 具有溢出效应的流感喷射市场(积极外部性)

p69.original: Societal Change as an Innovation Outcome
p69.zh: 社会变革作为一种创新成果

p70.original: Economist Carlota Perez draws on the lessons of past innovations to understand the current state of our economy. She demonstrates that prior technological turning points, such as the proliferation of railroads and the emergence of mass production, created initial periods of employment and wealth shifting but eventually led to greater well-being and economic growth. After difficult transition periods and sometimes economic meltdowns during the “installment” phase of widespread new technologies, many economies and the people within them have benefited from prolonged periods of economic and lifestyle improvement, including lower unemployment and better quality of life.
p70.zh: 经济学家卡洛塔·佩雷斯吸取了过去创新的经验教训,了解我国经济的现状。 她表明,以前的技术转折点,如铁路的扩散和大规模生产的出现,创造了就业和财富转移的最初时期,但最终导致了更大的福祉和经济增长。 在广泛的新技术的“安装”阶段,经历了困难的过渡期,有时经济崩溃,许多经济体及其人民从长期经济和生活方式的改善中受益,包括失业率降低和生活质量提高。

p71.original: Most prior innovation periods, such as the Industrial Revolution, had one significant downside: negative impacts on the environment, such as pollution and habitat destruction. Perez notes that our current revolution—in information and communications technology (ICT)—has the potential for significant positive externalities related to the environment. ICT is shifting many areas of society (and therefore industry) to digital experiences and services that do not require fossil fuels or similar natural resources. Vehicle sharing, product rental-reuse networks, and new manufacturing methods offer the promise of far less consumable consumption. And even though the appearance of delivery trucks and shipping boxes gives the impression of environmental damage, most studies indicate that online shopping is better for the environment than individuals shopping in person. (This is partly attributed to greater efficiency in a few trucks driving to a neighborhood rather than everyone in the neighborhood driving to several stores.) Consumers and governments can spur on those environmental benefits by choosing or partnering with companies that focus on furthering their environmental impact, such as by using solar power to fuel their computer servers or by using electrically powered delivery trucks.
p71.zh: 工业革命等大多数以前的创新时期都有一个重大的不利因素:对环境的不利影响,如污染和生境破坏。佩雷斯指出,我们目前进行的信息和通信技术革命有可能产生与环境有关的重大积极外差因素。信息和通信技术正在将社会的许多领域(因此也是工业领域)转向不需要化石燃料或类似自然资源的数字经验和服务。车辆共享、产品租赁-再使用网络和新的制造方法提供了消费量低得多的希望。 而尽管货车和运货箱的外观给人以环境破坏的印象,但大多数研究表明,在线购物对环境来说比个人亲自购物要好.消费者和政府可以通过选择或与那些注重进一步扩大其环境影响的公司合作,例如利用太阳能为其计算机服务器加油或使用电力输送卡车来刺激这些环境效益。

p72.original: Like other innovations, ICT has created some employment and economic opportunities while it has reduced others. Increased globalization and efficiencies have shuttered businesses and reduced wages in some areas. Perez’s research indicates that those types of employment shifts can be managed through proper regulation and investment (especially in human capital), particularly as firms in the relevant industries become mature and profitable. The prospects aren’t simple: ICT has created megafirms like Amazon and Apple, which despite pleasing their consumers can wield significant power over governments and employees. But on the environmental and societal front at least, ICT has offered a wealth of opportunities and externalities.
p72.zh: 与其他创新一样,信通技术也创造了一些就业和经济机会,同时减少了其他机会。全球化的加强和效率的提高,使一些领域的企业关闭,并降低了工资。佩雷斯的研究表明,可以通过适当的管理和投资(特别是在人力资本方面)来管理这些类型的就业转移,特别是在相关行业的公司变得成熟和有利可图的情况下。未来并不简单:信通技术已经创造了亚马逊和苹果等巨型企业,尽管它们让消费者对政府和员工拥有巨大的权力。 但至少在环境和社会方面,信通技术提供了大量的机会和外部条件。

p74.original: Competition creates pressure to innovate. However, if one can easily copy new inventions, then the original inventor loses the incentive to invest further in research and development. New technology often has positive externalities; that is, there are often spillovers from the invention of new technology that benefit firms other than the innovator. The social benefit of an invention, once the firm accounts for these spillovers, typically exceeds the private benefit to the inventor. If inventors could receive a greater share of the broader social benefits for their work, they would have a greater incentive to seek out new inventions.
p74.zh: 竞争给创新带来压力。 然而,如果一个人可以轻易地复制新的发明,那么原发明者就失去了进一步投资研发的动力.新技术往往具有积极的外在作用;即,发明新技术往往产生外溢效应,使创新者以外的公司受益。发明的社会福利,一旦公司对这些外溢效应负责,通常会超过发明人的个人福利。 如果发明者能够为自己的工作获得更大份额的更广泛的社会福利,他们就会有更大的动力去寻求新的发明。

p76.original: Do market demand curves reflect positive externalities? Why or why not?
p76.zh: 市场需求曲线是否反映了积极的外部效应? 为什么或为什么不呢?

p77.original: No. A market demand curve reflects only the private benefits of those who are consuming the product. Positive externalities are benefits that spill over to third parties, so they create social benefits, and are not captured by a market (or private benefit) demand curve.
p77.zh: 没有。市场需求曲线只反映消费该产品者的私人利益。积极的外在效应是溢给第三方的利益,因此产生社会效益,而不会被市场(或私人利益)需求曲线所抓住。

p78.original: Suppose that Sony's R&D investment in digital devices has increased profits by 20%. Is this a private or social benefit?
p78.zh: 假设索尼对数字设备的研发投资增加了20%的利润. 这是私人福利还是社会福利?

p79.original: Clearly Samsung is benefiting from the investment, so the 20% increase in profits is a private benefit. If Samsung is unable to capture all of the benefit, perhaps because other companies quickly copy and produce close substitutes, then Samsung’s investment will produce social benefits.
p79.zh: 三星显然从投资中受益,所以利润增加20%是私人利益. 如果三星无法掌握所有利益,也许因为其他公司迅速复制并生产近代产品,那么三星的投资将产生社会福利.

p80.original: The Gizmo Company is planning to develop new household gadgets.  shows the company’s demand for financial capital for research and development of these gadgets, based on expected rates of return from sales. Now, say that every investment would have an additional 5% social benefit—that is, an investment that pays at least a 6% return to the Gizmo Company will pay at least an 11% return for society as a whole; an investment that pays at least 7% for the Gizmo Company will pay at least 12% for society as a whole, and so on. Answer the questions that follow based on this information.
p80.zh: Gizmo公司正计划开发新的家用电器。 这表明该公司根据销售的预期收益率,需要金融资本来研究和开发这些电器。 现在,说每一笔投资都会带来5%的额外社会福利,也就是说,至少给Gizmo公司支付6%回报的投资,至少为整个社会支付11%回报;至少给Gizmo公司支付7%的投资,至少为整个社会支付12%,等等。回答根据这一信息提出的问题。

p99.zh: 如果持续利率为9%,如果Gizmo只从这种投资中获得私人利益,那么Gizmo将投资多少研发?

p100.original: Assume that the interest rate is still 9%. How much will the firm invest if it also receives the social benefits of its investment? (Add an additional 5% return on all levels of investment.)
p100.zh: 假设利率仍然是9%。 如果公司也从投资中获得社会效益,它将投资多少?(增加各级投资收益5%。 )

p103.original: The Junkbuyers Company travels from home to home, looking for opportunities to buy items that would otherwise end up with the garbage, but which the company can resell or recycle. Which will be larger, the private or the social benefits?
p103.zh: 容克买家公司从家到家,寻找机会购买本来会最终与垃圾一起,但公司可以转售或回收的物品.哪些是更大的,私人福利还是社会福利?

p104.original: When the Junkbuyers Company purchases something for resale, presumably both the buyer and the seller benefit—otherwise, they would not need to make the transaction. However, the company also reduces the amount of garbage produced, which saves money for households and/or for the city that disposes of garbage. So the social benefits are larger than the private benefits.
p104.zh: 如果容克买家公司购买了出售的东西,估计买方和卖方都受益——否则他们就不必进行交易。 然而,该公司也减少了生产的垃圾数量,这为家庭和(或)处理垃圾的城市节省了资金. 因此社会福利比私人福利还要大.

p106.zh: 公司在研发方面的投资如何产生积极的外部效应?

p107.zh: 如果没有外部利益,对研发的借贷和投资需求会更高还是更低?

p142.original: A number of different government policies can increase the incentives to innovate, including: guaranteeing intellectual property rights, government assistance with the costs of research and development, and cooperative research ventures between universities and companies.
p142.zh: 一些不同的政府政策可以增加创新的动力,包括:保障知识产权,政府提供研发费用方面的援助,以及大学和公司之间的合作研究项目。

p144.original: One way to increase new technology is to guarantee the innovator an exclusive right to that new product or process. Intellectual property rights include patents, which give the inventor the exclusive legal right to make, use, or sell the invention for a limited time, and copyright laws, which give the author an exclusive legal right over works of literature, music, film/video, and pictures. For example, if a pharmaceutical firm has a patent on a new drug, then no other firm can manufacture or sell that drug for 20 years, unless the firm with the patent grants permission. Without a patent, the pharmaceutical firm would have to face competition for any successful products, and could earn no more than a normal rate of profit. With a patent, a firm is able to earn monopoly profits on its product for a period of time—which offers an incentive for research and development. In general, how long can “a period of time” be? The Clear It Up discusses patent and copyright protection timeframes for some works you might know.
p144.zh: 增加新技术的一个办法是保证创新者对该新产品或工艺享有专属权利。知识产权包括专利,专利赋予发明人有限时间制作、使用或出售发明的专属法律权利,以及版权法,专利赋予作者对文学、音乐、电影/录像和图片作品的专属法律权利。 例如,如果制药公司对新药拥有专利,那么,除非专利公司准许,否则其他任何公司都不得制造或销售20年新药。 如果没有专利,制药公司将不得不面对任何成功产品的竞争,其收入不超过正常的利润率。有了专利,公司就可以在一段时间内获得对其产品的垄断利润——这为研发提供了动力。总的来说,“一段时期”可以持续多久?讨论一些你可能知道的作品的专利和版权保护时限。

p145.original: How long is Mickey Mouse protected from being copied?
p145.zh: 米奇老鼠被复制保护了多久?

p146.original: All patents and copyrights are scheduled to end someday. In 2003, copyright protection for Mickey Mouse was scheduled to run out. Once the copyright had expired, anyone would be able to copy Mickey Mouse cartoons or draw and sell new ones. In 1998, however, Congress passed the Sonny Bono Copyright Term Extension Act. For copyrights owned by companies or other entities, it increased or extended the copyright from 75 years to 95 years after publication. For copyrights owned by individuals, it increased or extended the copyright coverage from 50 years to 70 years after death. Along with protecting Mickey for another 20 years, the copyright extension affected about 400,000 books, movies, and songs.
p146.zh: 所有专利和版权都预定有一天会结束.2003年,米老鼠的版权保护被计划耗尽. 一旦版权到期,任何人都可以复制Mickey Mouse漫画或画和出售新漫画. 然而在1998年,国会通过了桑尼·博诺著作权期延长法. 对于公司或其他实体拥有的版权,其著作权在发布后从75年增加到95年,或予以扩大。 对于个人拥有的版权,其著作权覆盖范围从死亡后的50年增加到死亡后的70年或予以扩大.加上又保护了20年的米奇,版权扩展影响了约40万本书籍,电影,和歌曲.

p147.zh: 说明向美国提交的专利申请总数。专利和商标局,以及授予的专利总数,在1990年代中期随着互联网的发明而激增,今天仍然很强大.

p149.original: While patents provide an incentive to innovate by protecting the innovator, they are not perfect. For example:
p149.zh: 虽然专利通过保护创新者为创新提供了动力,但它们并不完美。 例如:

p150.original: In countries that already have patents, economic studies show that inventors receive only one-third to one-half of the total economic value of their inventions.
p150.zh: 在已经拥有专利的国家,经济研究表明发明者只获得其发明总经济价值的三分之一至一半.

p151.original: In a fast-moving high-technology industry like biotechnology or semiconductor design, patents may be almost irrelevant because technology is advancing so quickly.
p151.zh: 在生物技术或半导体设计等快速移动的高技术产业中,专利可能几乎无关紧要,因为技术进步如此之快.

p152.original: Not every new idea can be protected with a patent or a copyright—for example, a new way of organizing a factory or a new way of training employees.
p152.zh: 并不是每一个新想法都能用专利或版权来保护,例如,组织工厂的新方式或培训雇员的新方式。

p153.original: Patents may sometimes cover too much or be granted too easily. In the early 1970s, Xerox had received over 1,700 patents on various elements of the photocopy machine. Every time Xerox improved the photocopier, it received a patent on the improvement.
p153.zh: 专利有时可能涵盖过多,或者授予太容易。 在1970年代初,Xerox获得了1700多项关于复印机各种部件的专利. 每次Xerox改进复印机时,它都会获得关于改进的专利.

p154.original: The 20-year time period for a patent is somewhat arbitrary. Ideally, a patent should cover a long enough period of time for the inventor to earn a good return, but not so long that it allows the inventor to charge a monopoly price permanently.
p154.zh: 一项专利的20年期限有些武断。理想的情况是,专利应当涵盖足够长的时间,使发明人能够获得良好的回报,但不会持续到允许发明人永久收取垄断价格.

p155.original: Because patents are imperfect and do not apply well to all situations, alternative methods of improving the rate of return for inventors of new technology are desirable. The following sections describe some of these possible alternative policies.
p155.zh: 由于专利不完善,不能很好地适用于所有情况,因此,有必要采用其他方法提高新技术发明者的回报率。 以下各节介绍其中一些可能的替代政策。

p156.original: Policy #1: Government Spending on Research and Development
p156.zh: 政策1:政府在研究和发展方面的开支

p157.original: If the private sector does not have sufficient incentive to carry out research and development, one possibility is for the government to fund such work directly. Government spending can provide direct financial support for research and development (R&D) conducted at colleges and universities, nonprofit research entities, and sometimes by private firms, as well as at government-run laboratories. While government spending on research and development produces technology that is broadly available for firms to use, it costs taxpayers money and can sometimes be directed more for political than for scientific or economic reasons.
p157.zh: 如果私营部门没有充分的动力进行研究和开发,政府直接为这项工作提供资金是可能的。 政府开支可以为在大专院校、非营利研究实体、有时由私营公司以及政府开办的实验室开展的研究和开发活动提供直接的财政支助。 虽然政府在研究和开发方面的开支产生技术,供公司广泛使用,但它需要纳税人的钱,有时可以更多地用于政治,而不是科学或经济原因。

p158.original: Visit the NASA website and the USDA website to read about government research that would not take place were it left to firms, due to the externalities.
p158.zh: 访问美国航天局网站和USDA网站,了解由于外部因素,如果政府研究留给公司进行,则不会进行。

The third column shows that, relative to the total amount of funding, 22.7% comes from the federal government, about 69% of R&D is done by industry, and less than 4% is done by universities and colleges.  (The percentages below do not add up to exactly 100% due to rounding.)

p182.original: In the 1960s the federal government paid for about two-thirds of the nation’s R&D. Over time, the U.S. economy has come to rely much more heavily on industry-funded R&D. The federal government has tried to focus its direct R&D spending on areas where private firms are not as active. One difficulty with direct government support of R&D is that it inevitably involves political decisions about which projects are worthy. The scientific question of whether research is worthwhile can easily become entangled with considerations like the location of the congressional district in which the research funding is spent.
p182.zh: 在1960年代,联邦政府支付了全国三分之二的研发费用。随着时间的推移,美国经济开始更加依赖工业资助的研发。联邦政府试图将其直接研发支出集中在私营公司没有那么活跃的领域。 政府直接支持研发的一个困难是,这不可避免地涉及哪些项目值得作出政治决定。 关于研究是否值得的科学问题很容易与诸如研究经费所在的国会区位置等考虑纠缠在一起。

p183.original: Policy #2: Tax Breaks for Research and Development
p183.zh: 政策2:研究和发展的减税

p184.original: A complementary approach to supporting R&D that does not involve the government’s close scrutiny of specific projects is to give firms a reduction in taxes depending on how much research and development they do. The federal government refers to this policy as the research and experimentation (R&E) tax credit. According to the Treasury Department: “. . . the R&E Credit is also a cost-effective policy for stimulating additional private sector investment. Most recent studies find that each dollar of foregone tax revenue through the R&E Tax Credit causes firms to invest at least a dollar in R&D, with some studies finding a benefit to cost ratio of 2 or 2.96.”
p184.zh: 支持研发的一个补充办法,不涉及政府对具体项目的严密审查,就是根据企业的研发程度,给予企业减税优惠。联邦政府将这项政策称为研究和实验税抵免。财政部称:“......研发信贷也是刺激私营部门投资的一项具有成本效益的政策。 最近的研究发现,通过研究与评价税收抵免而放弃的税收每1美元会导致公司在研发方面至少投资1美元,一些研究发现其收益与成本比率为2或2.96。”

p185.original: Visit this website for more information on how the R&E Tax Credit encourages investment.
p185.zh: 访问该网站,了解研究与评估税收抵免如何鼓励投资。

p187.original: State and federal governments support research in a variety of ways. For example, United for Medical Research, a coalition of groups that seek funding for the National Institutes of Health, (which is supported by federal grants), states: “NIH-supported research added $69 billion to our GDP and supported seven million jobs in 2011 alone.” The United States remains the leading sponsor of medical-related research, spending $117 billion in 2011. Other institutions, such as the National Academy of Sciences and the National Academy of Engineering, receive federal grants for innovative projects. The Agriculture and Food Research Initiative (AFRI) at the United States Department of Agriculture awards federal grants to projects that apply the best science to the most important agricultural problems, from food safety to childhood obesity. Cooperation between government-funded universities, academies, and the private sector can spur product innovation and create whole new industries.
p187.zh: 州政府和联邦政府以各种方式支持研究工作。 例如,联合医疗研究组织(United for Medical Research)是一个为国家卫生研究所寻求资金的团体联盟(由联邦赠款支持),它指出:“NIH支持的研究增加了690亿美元的国内生产总值,仅在2011年就为700万个工作岗位提供了支持。” 美国仍然是与医疗有关的研究的主要赞助者,2011年花费了1,170亿美元。其他机构,如国家科学院和国家工程院,则接受联邦对创新项目的资助. 美国农业部的农业和粮食研究倡议(AFRI)向应用最佳科学处理从食品安全到儿童肥胖等最重要的农业问题的项目提供联邦赠款. 政府资助的大学、学院和私营部门之间的合作可以刺激产品创新和创造全新的产业。

p189.original: Public policy with regard to technology must often strike a balance. For example, patents provide an incentive for inventors, but they should be limited to genuinely new inventions and not extend forever.
p189.zh: 有关技术的公共政策往往必须取得平衡。 例如,专利为发明者提供了一种激励,但是专利应该限于真正的新发明,而不是永远延续.

p190.original: Government has a variety of policy tools for increasing the rate of return for new technology and encouraging its development, including: direct government funding of R&D, tax incentives for R&D, protection of intellectual property, and forming cooperative relationships between universities and the private sector.
p190.zh: 政府有各种政策工具来提高新技术的回报率和鼓励新技术的发展,包括:政府直接资助研发、为研发提供税收优惠、保护知识产权、在大学和私营部门之间建立合作关系。

p192.original: When residents in a neighborhood tidy it and keep it neat, there are a number of positive spillovers: higher property values, less crime, happier residents. What types of government policies can encourage neighborhoods to clean up?
p192.zh: 当邻居们整理和保持整洁时,会有一些积极的外溢效应:财产价值更高,犯罪减少,居民更快乐.哪些类型的政府政策可以鼓励邻里进行清理?

p193.original: Government programs that either pay for neighborhood clean-up directly or that provide reduced tax payments for those who clean up or fix up their own property could be enacted. It is also easy to imagine how a city might allow its businesses to form a group that would pay for and manage neighborhood cleanup.
p193.zh: 可以颁布政府方案,直接支付邻里清理费用,或向清理或修复自己财产者提供减税。也很容易想象一个城市如何允许其企业组成一个团体来支付和管理街区的清理。

p194.original: Education provides both private benefits to those who receive it and broader social benefits for the economy as a whole. Think about the types of policies a government can follow to address the issue of positive spillovers in technology and then suggest a parallel set of policies that governments could follow for addressing positive externalities in education.
p194.zh: 教育既向享受教育的人提供私人福利,也为整个经济提供更广泛的社会福利。考虑一下政府可以采取什么政策来解决技术方面的积极外溢问题,然后提出一套平行的政策,供政府处理教育方面的积极外溢。

p195.original: Government programs that either pay for education directly or that provide loans or reduced tax payments for education could create positive spillovers. A city might allow its businesses to form a group that would coordinate business efforts with schools and local colleges and universities—allowing students to obtain real-world experience in their chosen fields and providing businesses with enthusiastic, trained workers.
p195.zh: 政府方案要么直接支付教育费用,要么提供贷款,要么减少教育税收支付,这些都可能产生积极的外溢效应。 一个城市可能允许其企业组成一个小组,协调与学校和地方学院及大学的商业努力——允许学生在自己选择的领域获得现实世界的经验,并为企业提供热情和训练有素的工人。

p197.original: Why might private markets tend to provide too few incentives for the development of new technology?
p197.zh: 为什么私人市场为开发新技术提供激励的机会太少?

p198.original: What can government do to encourage the development of new technology?
p198.zh: 政府能做些什么来鼓励新技术的发展?

p200.zh: 政府必须参与支持对新技术的投资是否必然?

p208.original: Even though new technology creates positive externalities so that perhaps one-half or two-thirds of the social benefit of new inventions spills over to others, the inventor still receives some private return. What about a situation where the positive externalities are so extensive that private firms could not expect to receive any of the social benefit? We call this kind of good a public good. Spending on national defense is a good example of a public good. Let’s begin by defining the characteristics of a public good and discussing why these characteristics make it difficult for private firms to supply public goods. Then we will see how government may step in to address the issue.
p208.zh: 尽管新技术创造了积极的外在因素,使新发明的社会福利有一半或三分之二溢给他人,但发明者仍然得到一些私人回报。正面的外差因素如此广泛,以致私营公司无法指望获得任何社会福利,那么,这种情况怎么办? 我们称这种好事为公益.国防开支是公益事业的好例子. 让我们首先确定公益物的特征,并讨论这些特征为何使私营公司难以提供公益物。 然后我们将看看政府如何介入解决这个问题。

p209.original: The Definition of a Public Good

p210.original: Economists have a strict definition of a public good, and it does not necessarily include all goods financed through taxes. To understand the defining characteristics of a public good, first consider an ordinary private good, like a piece of pizza. We can buy and sell a piece of pizza fairly easily because it is a separate and identifiable item. However, public goods are not separate and identifiable in this way.
p210.zh: 经济学家对公益有一个严格的定义,不一定包括所有通过税收融资的商品. 为了了解公益物的决定性特征,首先考虑普通的私人物品,像披萨一样. 我们可以很容易地买和卖披萨 因为它是单独和可识别的物品。 然而,公共物品不是以这种方式分开和可识别的。

p211.original: Instead, public goods have two defining characteristics: they are nonexcludable and non-rival. The first characteristic, that a public good is nonexcludable, means that it is costly or impossible to exclude someone from using the good. If Larry buys a private good like a piece of pizza, then he can exclude others, like Lorna, from eating that pizza. However, if national defense is provided, then it includes everyone. Even if you strongly disagree with America’s defense policies or with the level of defense spending, the national defense still protects you. You cannot choose to be unprotected, and national defense cannot protect everyone else and exclude you.
p211.zh: 相反,公益物有两个决定性的特征:它们不可排斥,不可竞争。 第一个特征是,公共物品是不可排除的,这意味着将某人排除在该物品的使用范围之外是昂贵的或不可能的。 如果Larry买到像披萨一样的私人物品,那么他可以排除其他人,如Lorna,吃那披萨. 然而,如果提供国防,那么它包括每个人. 即使你强烈反对美国的国防政策或国防开支水平,国防仍然保护你. 你不能选择不受保护 国防不能保护其他人 也不能排斥你

p212.original: The second main characteristic of a public good, that it is non-rival, means that when one person uses the public good, another can also use it. With a private good like pizza, if Max is eating the pizza then Michelle cannot also eat it; that is, the two people are rivals in consumption. With a public good like national defense, Max’s consumption of national defense does not reduce the amount left for Michelle, so they are non-rival in this area.
p212.zh: 公益品的第二个主要特征是非竞争性,这意味着当一个人使用公益品时,另一个人也可以使用.有了比萨饼这样的私人物品,如果马克思在吃比萨饼,那么米歇尔也不能吃;也就是说,两人在消费上是竞争对手. 由于国防这样的公益,马克思对国防的消耗并没有减少留给米歇尔的金额,因此他们在该地区是非竞争的.

p213.original: A number of government services are examples of public goods. For instance, it would not be easy to provide fire and police service so that some people in a neighborhood would be protected from the burning and burglary of their property, while others would not be protected at all. Protecting some necessarily means protecting others, too.
p213.zh: 一些政府服务是公益物的例子。 例如,提供消防和警察服务并不容易,这样,邻近地区的一些人的财产不会被烧毁和盗窃,而其他人则完全得不到保护。保护一些人也必然意味着保护其他人。

p214.original: Positive externalities and public goods are closely related concepts. Public goods have positive externalities, like police protection or public health funding. Not all goods and services with positive externalities, however, are public goods. Investments in education have huge positive spillovers but can be provided by a private company. Private companies can invest in new inventions such as the Apple iPad and reap profits that may not capture all of the social benefits. We can also describe patents as an attempt to make new inventions into private goods, which are excludable and rivalrous, so that no one but the inventor can use them during the length of the patent.
p214.zh: 积极的外在因素和公益物是密切相关的概念。公益物具有积极的外在作用,例如警察保护或公共卫生资金。 然而,并非所有具有积极外部效应的货物和服务都是公益品。教育投资具有巨大的积极外溢效应,但可由私营公司提供。私人公司可以投资苹果iPad等新发明,并收获可能无法捕捉到所有社会福利的利润. 我们还可以将专利描述为试图将新的发明变成私人商品,这些物品是不可排除的,相互竞争的,这样,除了发明者之外,没有人可以在专利的长度期间使用它们.

p215.original: The Free Rider Problem of Public Goods

p216.original: Private companies find it difficult to produce public goods. If a good or service is nonexcludable, like national defense, so that it is impossible or very costly to exclude people from using this good or service, then how can a firm charge people for it?
p216.zh: 私营公司发现难以生产公益物。 如果一件好事或一件服务是不可排除的,比如国防,以致于排除人们使用这种物品或服务是不可能的或非常昂贵的,那么一个坚定的单位怎么能向人们收费呢?

p217.original: Visit this website to read about a connection between free riders and “bad music.”
p217.zh: 访问该网站,了解自由骑手与“坏音乐”之间的联系。

p218.original: When individuals make decisions about buying a public good, a free rider problem can arise, in which people have an incentive to let others pay for the public good and then to “free ride” on the purchases of others. We can express the free rider problem in terms of the prisoner’s dilemma game, which we discussed as a representation of oligopoly in Monopolistic Competition and Oligopoly.
p218.zh: 当个人决定购买公益物时,就会产生自由骑手问题,人们有动机让他人为公益物付费,然后“免费骑车”购买他人。 我们可以用囚犯困境游戏来表达自由骑手的问题,我们讨论过这个游戏是垄断竞争和奥利戈波利的寡头垄断的代表。

p219.original: There is a dilemma with the Prisoner’s Dilemma, though. See the Work It Out feature.
p219.zh: 囚犯的困境也存在两难境地。参见"Work It Out"的功能.

p220.original: The Problem with the Prisoner’s Dilemma

p221.original: Suppose two people, Rachel and Samuel, are considering purchasing a public good. The difficulty with the prisoner’s dilemma arises as each person thinks through their strategic choices.
p221.zh: 假设瑞秋和塞缪尔两人考虑购买公益品.囚犯困境的难处是每个人通过自己的战略选择来思考的。

p222.original: Step 1. Rachel reasons in this way: If Samuel does not contribute, then I would be a fool to contribute. However, if Samuel does contribute, then I can come out ahead by not contributing.
p222.zh: 步骤1。瑞秋这样的理由:如果塞缪尔不捐款,那么我就会傻傻地捐款. 然而,如果塞缪尔确实有贡献,那么我可以不贡献而出面.

p223.original: Step 2. Either way, I should choose not to contribute, and instead hope that I can be a free rider who uses the public good paid for by Samuel.
p223.zh: 步骤二. 无论哪种方式,我都应该选择不作出贡献,而希望我能够成为一个自由骑手,利用塞缪尔所付的公益物.

p224.original: Step 3. Samuel reasons the same way about Rachel.
p224.zh: 步骤3。塞缪尔对瑞秋也有同样的理由.

p225.original: Step 4. When both people reason in that way, the public good never gets built, and there is no movement to the option where everyone cooperates—which is actually best for all parties.
p225.zh: 步骤4。 当两人都以这种方式来解释, 公众利益就永远无法建立,

p226.original: The Role of Government in Paying for Public Goods
p226.zh: 政府在支付公益金方面的作用

p227.original: The key insight in paying for public goods is to find a way of assuring that everyone will make a contribution and to prevent free riders. For example, if people come together through the political process and agree to pay taxes and make group decisions about the quantity of public goods, they can defeat the free rider problem by requiring, through the law, that everyone contributes.
p227.zh: 支付公益金的关键见解是找到一种方法,确保每个人都能作出贡献,并防止自由骑手。 例如,如果人们通过政治进程走到一起,同意缴纳税款,并就公益物的数量作出集体决定,那么他们可以通过法律要求每个人作出贡献来打败自由骑手问题.

p228.original: However, government spending and taxes are not the only way to provide public goods. In some cases, markets can produce public goods. For example, think about radio. It is nonexcludable, since once the radio signal is broadcast, it would be very difficult to stop someone from receiving it. It is non-rival, since one person listening to the signal does not prevent others from listening as well. Because of these features, it is practically impossible to charge listeners directly for listening to conventional radio broadcasts.
p228.zh: 然而,政府开支和税收并不是提供公益品的唯一途径。在某些情况下,市场可以生产公益物。 比如说,想想收音机 它不可排除,因为一旦无线电信号被广播,就很难阻止有人接收它. 这是非竞争性的,因为一个人听信号并不妨碍其他人也听。 由于这些特点,几乎不可能直接向听众收取收听传统无线电广播的费用。

p229.original: Radio has found a way to collect revenue by selling advertising, which is an indirect way of “charging” listeners by taking up some of their time. Ultimately, consumers who purchase the goods advertised are also paying for the radio service, since the station builds in the cost of advertising into the product cost. In a more recent development, satellite radio companies, such as SiriusXM, charge a regular subscription fee for streaming music without commercials. In this case, however, the product is excludable—only those who pay for the subscription will receive the broadcast.
p229.zh: 电台找到了一种通过出售广告来收税的方法,这是“收费”听众的一种间接方式,占用了他们的一些时间。最终,购买广告商品的消费者也支付广播服务费用,因为电台将广告成本计入产品成本。 在更近的发展中,天狼星XM等卫星无线电公司对没有商业广告的流媒体音乐收取定期订阅费. 然而,在这种情况下,产品是不可排除的——只有那些支付订阅费的人才能接受广播。

p230.original: Some public goods will also have a mixture of public provision at no charge along with fees for some purposes, like a public city park that is free to use, but the government charges a fee for parking your car, for reserving certain picnic grounds, and for food sold at a refreshment stand.
p230.zh: 有些公共物品也会免费提供公共物品, 以及某些用途的收费, 例如公共城市公园可以免费使用, 但政府会收取停车费、 保留某些野餐场地费、 以及餐饮摊出售的食物。

p231.original: Read this article to find out what economists say the government should pay for.
p231.zh: 读这篇文章,看看经济学家说政府应该付出什么代价.

p232.original: In other cases, we can use social pressures and personal appeals, rather than the force of law, to reduce the number of free riders and to collect resources for the public good. For example, neighbors sometimes form an association to carry out beautification projects or to patrol their area after dark to discourage crime. In low-income countries, where social pressure strongly encourages all farmers to participate, farmers in a region may come together to work on a large irrigation project that will benefit all. We can view many fundraising efforts, including raising money for local charities and for the endowments of colleges and universities, as an attempt to use social pressure to discourage free riding and to generate the outcome that will produce a public benefit.
p232.zh: 在其他情况下,我们可以利用社会压力和个人呼吁,而不是法律的力量,减少自由骑手的数量,为公益目的筹集资源. 例如,邻居有时会组成一个协会,实施美化项目,或在天黑后巡逻,劝阻犯罪。 在低收入国家,社会压力强烈鼓励所有农民参与,一个区域的农民可以聚集一堂,共同开展一个惠及所有人的大型灌溉项目。 我们可以认为,许多筹资努力,包括为地方慈善机构以及大专院校的捐赠筹集资金,是利用社会压力阻止自由骑马和产生将带来公共利益的成果的尝试。

p233.original: Common Resources and the “Tragedy of the Commons”

p234.original: There are some goods that do not fall neatly into the categories of private good or public good. While it is easy to classify a pizza as a private good and a city park as a public good, what about an item that is nonexcludable and rivalrous, such as the queen conch?
p234.zh: 有些货物并不完全属于私人货物或公共货物类别。 虽然将披萨归类为私人物品和城市公园归类为公益品很容易,但像王后海螺这样的不可排斥和竞争的物品呢?

p235.original: In the Caribbean, the queen conch is a large marine mollusk that lives in shallow waters of sea grass. These waters are so shallow, and so clear, that a single diver may harvest many conch in a single day. Not only is conch meat a local delicacy and an important part of the local diet, but artists use the large ornate shells and craftsmen transform them. Because almost anyone with a small boat, snorkel, and mask, can participate in the conch harvest, it is essentially nonexcludable. At the same time, fishing for conch is rivalrous. Once a diver catches one conch another diver cannot catch it.
p235.zh: 在加勒比海地区,海螺王后是一种大型的海洋软体动物,生活在海草的浅水中. 这些水域很浅,很清澈,以至于一个单一的潜水员可能在一天内收获许多海螺.不仅海螺肉是当地精美的,也是当地饮食的重要组成部分,艺术家们还使用大圆果壳,工匠来改造它们. 因为几乎所有拥有小船,吸水器,面具的人都可以参加海螺的收割,所以基本上不可排除. 同时,钓海螺也具有竞争性. 一旦一个潜水员抓到一只海螺 另一只潜水员就无法抓到它

p236.original: We call goods that are nonexcludable and rivalrous common resources. Because the waters of the Caribbean are open to all conch fishermen, and because any conch that you catch is a conch that I cannot catch, fishermen tend to overharvest common resources like the conch.
p236.zh: 我们称之为不可排斥和相互竞争的共同资源。 因为加勒比海的水域向所有海螺渔民开放,而且因为任何你捕获的海螺都是我无法捕获的海螺,因此渔民往往过度捕捞像海螺这样的共同资源.

p237.original: The problem of overharvesting common resources is not a new one, but ecologist Garret Hardin put the tag “tragedy of the commons” to the problem in a 1968 article in the magazine Science. Economists view this as a problem of property rights. Since nobody owns the ocean, or the conch that crawl on the sand beneath it, no one individual has an incentive to protect that resource and responsibly harvest it. To address the issue of overharvesting conch and other marine fisheries, economists have advocated simple devices like fishing licenses, harvest limits, and shorter fishing seasons. One approach that has been turned to more recently is the implementation of catch shares, whereby regulators establish a total allowable catch, and then fishermen are allocated a portion of that total allowable catch. Catch shares appear to slow the race to fish. When the population of a species drops to critically low numbers, governments have even banned the harvest until biologists determine that the population has returned to sustainable levels. In fact, such is the case with the conch, the harvesting of which the government has effectively banned in the United States since 1986.
p237.zh: 过度采伐共同资源的问题并不是一个新问题,但生态学家加勒特·哈丁在杂志《科学》1968年的一篇文章中将“共同资源的愤怒”贴上了这个问题的标签。经济学家认为这是财产权问题。 由于没有人拥有海洋, 或爬在它下面的沙子上的海螺, 没有人有动力保护这种资源, 并负责任地收获它。 为了解决过度捕捞海螺和其他海洋渔业的问题,经济学家主张采用诸如捕捞许可证、捕捞限额和较短的捕捞季节等简单装置。 最近采用的一种方法是实施渔获量份额,根据这种办法,监管机构确定总可捕量,然后将渔民分配到总可捕量的一部分。捕捉股份似乎减缓了钓鱼的竞速速度. 当一个物种的数量下降到极低的水平时,政府甚至禁止收获,直到生物学家确定该物种人口已恢复到可持续水平。 事实上,海螺就是这种情况,自1986年以来,美国政府实际上禁止了海螺的收获。

p238.original: The tragedy of the commons is a frequent economic and social framework for discussions about a range of common resources, even extending into digital resources such as open media repositories and online libraries. Prominent economist Elinor Ostrom, the first woman to receive the Nobel Prize in Economics, proposed an alternate version, sometimes referred to as the "non-tragedy of the commons." After extensive fieldwork in areas as diverse as Indonesia, Kenya, Maine (U.S.), and Nepal, she challenged the notion that people would only avoid depletion of common resources if they were forced to by regulatory laws and property rights. She noted that farmers working shared land could communicate and cooperate in order to maximize and preserve the fields over time. She argued that when those who benefit most from a resource are in close proximity to it (like a farm field that directly serves a town), the resource is better managed without external influence.
p238.zh: 公域的悲剧是讨论一系列共同资源的一个频繁的经济和社会框架,甚至扩展到数字资源,如开放的媒体寄存器和在线图书馆。著名的经济学家埃利诺·奥斯特罗姆(Elinor Ostrom)是第一位获得诺贝尔经济学奖的女性,她提出了一个替代版本,有时被称为"公有制的非暴利". 在印尼,肯尼亚,缅因(美国),尼泊尔等多个不同的领域进行了广泛的实地工作后,她对人们只有在受到监管法律和财产权的强迫的情况下才会避免共同资源耗尽的观念提出质疑. 她指出,从事共有土地工作的农民可以进行交流与合作,以便随着时间的推移最大限度地扩大和保护农田。 她认为,当资源受益最大的人离资源很近时(像一个直接服务于城镇的农田),在没有外部影响的情况下,资源的管理更好.

p239.original: Visit this website for more on the queen conch industry.
p239.zh: 访问这个网站 更多关于王后海螺产业。

p240.original: Positive Externalities in Public Health Programs
p240.zh: 公共卫生方案的积极外差因素

p241.original: One of the most remarkable changes in the standard of living in the last several centuries is that people are living longer. Scientists believe that, thousands of years ago, human life expectancy ranged between 20 to 30 years. By 1900, average life expectancy in the United States was 47 years. By 2015, life expectancy was 79 years; due to COVID-19, life expectancy declined slightly to 77 years in 2020. Most of the gains in life expectancy in the history of the human race happened in the twentieth century.
p241.zh: 在过去几个世纪里,生活水平最显著的变化之一是人们活得更长。科学家认为,数千年前,人类的预期寿命介于20至30岁之间. 到1900年,美国的平均预期寿命为47岁. 到2015年,预期寿命为79岁;由于COVID-19,2020年的预期寿命略有下降至77岁.人类历史上预期寿命的提高大部分发生在20世纪.

p242.original: The rise in life expectancy seems to stem from three primary factors. First, systems for providing clean water and disposing of human waste helped to prevent the transmission of many diseases. Second, changes in public behavior have advanced health. Early in the twentieth century, for example, people learned the importance of boiling bottles before using them for food storage and baby’s milk, washing their hands, and protecting food from flies. More recent behavioral changes include reducing the number of people who smoke tobacco and precautions to limit sexually transmitted diseases. Third, medicine has played a large role. Scientists developed immunizations for diphtheria, cholera, pertussis, tuberculosis, tetanus, and yellow fever between 1890 and 1930. Penicillin, discovered in 1941, led to a series of other antibiotic drugs for bringing infectious diseases under control. In recent decades, drugs that reduce the risks of high blood pressure have had a dramatic effect in extending lives.
p242.zh: 预期寿命的提高似乎来自三个主要因素。 第一,提供清洁水和处理人类废物的制度有助于防止许多疾病的传播。 第二,公共行为的变化已经提高了健康水平。 例如,在二十世纪初,人们在使用沸瓶储存食物和婴儿牛奶、洗手以及保护食物免受苍蝇伤害之前就已经认识到了沸瓶的重要性。 最近的行为变化包括减少吸烟者的人数和采取预防措施限制性传染疾病. 第三,医学发挥了很大的作用。科学家在1890年至1930年间开发了白喉,霍乱,百日咳,肺结核,破伤风,黄热病的免疫.1941年发现的青霉素导致了一系列其他抗生素药物,用于控制传染病.近几十年来,减少高血压风险的药物对延长寿命产生了巨大影响.

p243.original: These advances in public health have all been closely linked to positive externalities and public goods. Public health officials taught hygienic practices to mothers in the early 1900s and encouraged less smoking in the late 1900s. Government funded many public sanitation systems and storm sewers because they have the key traits of public goods. In the twentieth century, many medical discoveries emerged from government or university-funded research. Patents and intellectual property rights provided an additional incentive for private inventors. The reason for requiring immunizations, phrased in economic terms, is that it prevents spillovers of illness to others—as well as helping the person immunized.
p243.zh: 公共卫生方面的这些进步都与积极的外在因素和公益物密切相关。公共卫生官员在1900年代初向母亲传授卫生习惯,并在1900年代末鼓励少吸烟. 政府资助了许多公共环卫系统和下水道,因为它们具有公益品的主要特征。 在20世纪,许多医学发现都来自政府或大学资助的研究.专利和知识产权为私人发明人提供了额外的奖励。要求免疫(用经济术语来说)的原因是,它防止疾病蔓延到他人——以及帮助接受免疫的人。

p244.original: The Benefits of Voyager I Endure

p245.original: While we applaud the technology spillovers of NASA’s space projects, we should also acknowledge that those benefits are not shared equally. Economists like Tyler Cowen, a professor at George Mason University, are seeing increasing evidence of a widening gap between those who have access to rapidly improving technology, and those who do not. According to Cowen, author of the 2013 book, Average Is Over: Powering America Beyond the Age of the Great Stagnation, this inequality in access to technology and information is going to deepen the inequality in skills, and ultimately, in wages and global standards of living.
p245.zh: 虽然我们赞赏美国航天局空间项目的技术外溢效应,但我们也应该承认,这些好处不是平等分享的。乔治·梅森大学教授泰勒·考恩(Tyler Cowen)等经济学家看到越来越多的证据表明,获得迅速改进技术的人与没有获得技术的人之间的差距正在扩大。 根据2013年著作《平均超越:让美国超越大停滞时代》的作者科恩(Cowen)的说法,在获取技术和信息方面的这种不平等将加深技能方面的不平等,并最终加深工资和全球生活水平方面的不平等。

p247.original: A public good has two key characteristics: it is nonexcludable and non-rival. Nonexcludable means that it is costly or impossible for one user to exclude others from using the good. Non-rival means that when one person uses the good, it does not prevent others from using it. Markets often have a difficult time producing public goods because free riders will attempt to use the public good without paying for it. One can overcome the free rider problem through measures to assure that users of the public good pay for it. Such measures include government actions, social pressures, and specific situations where markets have discovered a way to collect payments.
p247.zh: 公益物有两个关键特征:不可排斥和非竞争性。不可排除意味着,一个用户将其他人排除在使用商品之外是昂贵的或不可能的。 非竞争是指当一个人使用善时,并不阻止其他人使用.市场往往很难生产公益物,因为自由骑手会试图使用公益物而不花钱. 人们可以通过采取措施确保公益的使用者为此付出代价来克服免费骑车者的问题。 这些措施包括政府行动、社会压力和市场发现收取付款方式的具体情况。

p249.original: Which of the following goods or services are nonexcludable?
p249.zh: 下列哪些货物或服务是不可排除的?

p251.original: streaming music from satellite transmission programs
p251.zh: 来自卫星传输程序的流传音乐

p255.original: Once citizens are protected from crime, it is difficult to exclude someone from this protection, so it is nonexcludable.
p255.zh: 一旦公民免受犯罪侵害,就很难将某人排除在这种保护之外,因此,这种保护是不可排除的。

p256.original: Some satellite radio services, such as SiriusXM, are sold by subscription fee, so it is excludable.
p256.zh: 一些卫星无线电服务,如天狼星XM,通过订阅费出售,因此可以排除.

p257.original: Once a road is built it is difficult to exclude people, although toll roads can exclude non-payers.
p257.zh: 公路建成后,很难排除人,虽然收费公路可以排除非付费人.

p258.original: Primary education can be provided by private companies and so it is excludable.
p258.zh: 初等教育可以由私营公司提供,因此是不可排除的。

p259.original: Companies sell cell phone service and exclude those who do not pay.
p259.zh: 公司销售手机服务,不付费的除外.

p260.original: Are the following goods non-rival in consumption?
p260.zh: 下列商品是否在消费中无竞争地位?

p265.original: Two people cannot enjoy the same slice of pizza at the same time, so private goods, such as a slice of pizza, are rivalrous.
p265.zh: 两个人不能同时享受同样的披萨片,因此私人商品,如披萨片,是竞争对手的.

p266.original: Two people cannot use one laptop at the same time, so they are rivalrous in consumption.
p266.zh: 两人不能同时使用一台笔记本电脑,因此在消费上是竞争对手.

If Becky decides not to clean and Sarah does all the cleaning, then Sarah spends 10 hours cleaning (Becky spends 0) but Sarah is exhausted. The same would occur for Becky if Sarah decided not to clean—Becky spends 10 hours and becomes exhausted. If both girls decide not to clean, they both have a dirty room.

c0.original: Launched by NASA on September 5, 1977, Voyager I’s primary mission was to provide detailed images of Jupiter, Saturn, and their moons. It took this photograph of Jupiter on its journey. In August of 2012, Voyager I entered interstellar space—the first human-made object to do so—and it is expected to send data and images back to earth until 2025. c1.original: Big Drug faces a cost of borrowing of 8%. If the firm receives only the private benefits of investing in R&D, then we show its demand curve for financial capital by DPrivate, and the equilibrium will occur at $30 million. Because there are spillover benefits, society would find it optimal to have $52 million of investment. If the firm could keep the social benefits of its investment for itself, its demand curve for financial capital would be DSocial and it would be willing to borrow $52 million.
c1.zh: 大毒品面临8%的借贷成本. 如果公司只获得对研发投资的私人利益,那么我们就会显示DPrivate对金融资本的需求曲线,平衡将达到3000万美元. 由于有溢出效应的好处,社会会发现拥有5200万美元的投资是最佳的. 如果公司能够为自己保留投资的社会效益,其对金融资本的需求曲线将是DSocial,它愿意借款5 200万美元。

c3.original: The market demand curve does not reflect the positive externality of flu vaccinations, so only QMarket will be exchanged. This outcome is inefficient because the marginal social benefit exceeds the marginal social cost. If the government provides a subsidy to consumers of flu shots, equal to the marginal social benefit minus the marginal private benefit, the level of vaccinations can increase to the socially optimal quantity of QSocial.
c3.zh: 市场需求曲线并不反映流感疫苗的正外向性,因此只有QMarket才会进行交换. 这一结果效率低下,因为边际社会福利超过边际社会成本. 如果政府向流感疫苗的消费者提供补贴,相当于边际社会福利减去边际私人福利,那么接种疫苗的水平可以提高到社会最佳的QSocial数量.

c4.original: The number of applications filed for patents increased substantially beginning in the 1990s, due in part to the invention of the internet. The internet led to many other inventions, but also made it much easier to copy, steal, or "pirate" intellectual property, which led to the 1998 Copyright Term Extension Act. (Source: http://www.uspto.gov/web/offices/ac/ido/oeip/taf/us_stat.htm)
c4.zh: 申请专利的数量从1990年代开始大幅增加,部分原因是互联网的发明。互联网带来了许多其他的发明,但也使得复制,窃取,或"盗版"知识产权更容易,这导致了1998年的版权期限延长法.(资料来源:http://www.uspto.gov/web/offices/ac/ido/oeip/taf/us_stat.htm).
